messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent - thanks for posting the new version, but I am still getting an error - now when it gets to part 3.

This is the error I get, and it seems to be related to the package 'zoo' that is called in for the interpolations:

Error in approx(wix, unlist(object[wix]), xout = wrng) :
  need at least two non-NA values to interpolate

Do you have any leads on what is going on or ho to fix it?
Thanks

Diego Bassani

> I have uploaded GGIR version 1.5-3 with some bug fixes last night, introduced in version 1.5-1 I uploaded last week.

> - Error in g.readaccfile(filename = datafile, blocksize = blocksize, blocknumber = i,  :  object 'P' not found".
> - Error in as.matrix(deci$rawxyz) : object 'deci' not found => in relation to g.wavread

>
> I also added some contributing guidelines at https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR
>
> Thanks, and sorry for the inconvenience the recent bugs may have caused.
>
> Vincent
>
>
>

> > GGIR version 1.5-1 now online with a few important updates:

> >
> > For those interested in seeing the underlying code and contributing: I copied the GGIR github repo from the ucl github organisation where it has lived for the past year to a new neutral github organisation I recently created: https://github.com/wadpac.
> >
> > For the latest overview of GGIR related publications see here <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/wiki/Publication-list>. Please email me when you spot a new publication that is not on the list yet.
> >
> > Thanks, Vincent
> >

Dear all,

GGIR version 1.5-7
The cwa read functionality that was introduced in version 1.5-3 had a bug, this has been fixed for 1.5-7, which is on CRAN now. Windows binaries will follow soon. Note that it is important to restart R in order for this update to become active. If you are not looking at cwa data, then don't worry about this, because the rest of the package has remained unchanged.

Issue reports
>From now onwards I would appreciate if you could post your issues in the issue tracker of the GGIR github repository <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues>. If you are new to github: Github accounts are free. Using github issues will make it easier for me to keep track of your issues, it will make it easier for others to help me help you, and it will reduce the traffic in this mailing list.

On a side note - Once you have a github account don't forgot to click on the star at the top of the GGIR repository <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR>, this is the software developer's equivalent of the h-index for scientists. So, if you like GGIR then please click the star :)

I will continue using this google group / email list to inform you about new releases of GGIR and other news of general interest

Package vignette development ongoing
I have made some big expansions to the package vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html>.
It seems that various users have been developing their own tutorials and standard operating procedures, hopefully the vignette can act as a useful reference point for all.

Thanks, Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Khai,

Estimating time spent in MVPA is one of the big mysteries in physical activity research.
For threshold selection there is some guidance in the literature, but more difficult is the decision on how to define a MVPA bout and how to mathematically allow for gaps in bouts when the epochs are shorter than 1 minute.
There is no gold standard for this, by which any approach could in theory be the 'right' one. It is then all down to your interpretation of the estimates.

You may want to read papers that have used the MVPA estimates, e.g. da Silva in IJE 2014 <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25361583> and Menai in Sci Rep 2017 <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28367987>. Further, the GGIR documentation should clarify what all the variables mean.

Vincent
